The starting compound is 2-formyl-5-vinylcyclohex-3-enecarboxylic acid. Its molecular formula is C₁₀H₁₂O₃, with an index of hydrogen deficiency (IHD) of 5 (one ring, three carbonyl/alkene double bonds, and one additional ring double bond). 

Reaction with red phosphorus and excess HI is a powerful reduction that removes all oxygen atoms and reduces all alkenes to alkanes. Specifically:
- The carboxylic acid (–COOH) is reduced to a methyl group (–CH₃).
- The formyl group (–CHO) is reduced to a methyl group (–CH₃).
- The vinyl group (–CH=CH₂) is reduced to an ethyl group (–CH₂CH₃).
- The cyclohexene ring double bond is reduced to a single bond, giving a cyclohexane ring.

The product is a fully saturated cyclohexane ring with three alkyl substituents, giving a molecular formula of C₁₀H₂₀. A saturated cyclic hydrocarbon has one degree of unsaturation due to the ring, so its IHD is 1.
